ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: This is a food web diagram, containing labels such as Algae, Tiny Shrimps, Butterfly Fish, Limpets, Periwinkles, Snails, Crabs, Cuttlefish, Sea Urchins, etc. In the middle right side of the diagram there is a box labeled “Crabs”. It can be seen that arrows point from “Snails” to “Crabs”, from “Sea Urchins” to “Crabs”, and there is an arrow pointing from “Crabs” to “Cuttlefish”. Reasoning: In a food web, arrows usually indicate the direction of energy flow, that is, from the organism being eaten to the organism that eats it. Therefore, the arrows pointing to “Crabs” indicate that crabs eat these organisms, and crabs are predators in these relationships. The question asks “What is a predator?”, and the singular-form answer is crab.
